questions.question: 'Yakshagana' is associated with which of the following states?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Yakshagana is a traditional Indian theatre form, developed in Karnataka.
 
• It combines dance, music, dialogue, costume, make-up, and stage techniques with a unique style and form.
 
• It is believed to have evolved from pre-classical music and theatre during the period of the Bhakti.
 
• Most of the stories in yakshagana are drawn from the epics like Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavatha and other mythological episodes.
 
• Yakshagana literally means, “song” of the yaksha or music of celestial beings.
 
• The mela or troupe consists of two main parts:
 
 
• Mummela (foreground actors)
 
• Himmela (singers and instrumentalists in the background).
 
 
 
• Theyyam is also a manifestation of Bhutha worship.
 
• ​Yakshagana is believed to have evolved from the ancient Bhutha-worship prevalent in Dakshina Kannada and Kasaragod.

 
• It is known that two variants of Yakshagana exist. The characteristics or features of these two different styles of Yakshagana are listed below:
 
 
• ​**Badagu Thittu (Northern Style):**

 
 
• Originates in the northern regions of Karnataka, including Udupi and North Kannada districts.
 
• Known for its dynamic and vigorous dance movements.
 
• Features more rhythmic footwork and elaborate expressions.
 
• Emphasis on narrative singing and dialogues.
 
• Instruments used: Maddale (drum), Chende (cylindrical drum), and Harmonium.
 
 
 
• **Thenku Thittu (Southern Style):**
 
 
• Predominantly practiced in the southern parts of Karnataka and Kasaragod in Kerala.
 
• Characterized by smooth and graceful dance movements.

• Costumes and ornaments are generally more vibrant and ornamental.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian Constitution mentions 'Special address by the Governor to the State Legislature'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 176**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 176**

 
 
• Article 176 of the Constitution of India deals with a special address by the Governor.
 
• The Governor comes under Article 153 to 167 in Part VI of the constitution.
 
• The government is appointed by the president.
 
• The governor is the chief executive head of the state.
 
• 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 facilitated the appointment of the same person as a Governor for two or more States.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** ****Article 171**

 
 
• Article 171 of the Indian Constitution deals with the composition of the Legislative Councils.
 
• The Legislative Council is the upper house in those states of India that have a bicameral legislature.
 
• According to Article 171, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a state shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that state.
 
• The members of the Legislative Council are elected by various groups including the Legislative Assembly, graduates, teachers, and local authority members.
 
• The Governor of the state also nominates some members to the Legislative Council.
 
 
 
• **Article 175**
 
 
• Article 175 of the Indian Constitution mentions the right of the Governor to address and to send messages to the House (or Houses) of the state legislature.
 
• This article empowers the Governor to communicate with the state legislature, ensuring a channel for the executive to convey important messages or addresses.
 
• The Governor can address the state legislature at the commencement of each session and can send messages to either House of the legislature.
 
• The Houses are required to consider any matter the Governor addresses or sends as a message.
 
 
 
• **Article 173**
 
 
• Article 173 of the Indian Constitution "Qualification for membership of the State Legislature" deals with the State Government.
 
• The purpose of article 173(a) of the Constitution is to ensure that any person, who wants to be a member of Legislature of a State, must bear true faith and allegiance to the Constitution of India as by law established and undertake to uphold the sovereignty and integrity of India, and, to ensure this, he must make an oath or affirmation.
 
• The article does not mention that the making of oath or affirmation is to be preliminary to the validity of candidature in each constituency, and recognizes the fact that, once the necessary qualification is obtained, that qualification removes the bar laid down by that article.

• Dry Ice

 
 
• Dry ice is simply carbon dioxide that has been cooled and condensed.
 
• When it reaches ambient temperature and pressure, it bypasses the melting process and expands directly into carbon dioxide gas.
 
• Dry ice is made by compressing and cooling gaseous CO2under high pressure, resulting in liquid CO2.
 
• Dry ice is frequently used as a substitute for refrigeration for groceries and medical supplies due to its exceptionally low temperature of -78.C
 
 
 
• Uses of Dry Ice
 
 
• Dry ice is used to keep the sensitive asphalt at the proper temperature during transportation from the manufacturing factory to the job site.
 
• During breakdowns, use dry ice to keep the contents of the refrigerator cool.
 
• Dry ice is the most efficient and cost-effective way of keeping perishables cooled or frozen.
